observation.visible_scene: Dense green rainforest canopy fills the frame, with a BBC logo fixed at top-left. A proboscis monkey (orange-brown torso, pale elongated limbs and long tail, prominent nose) is suspended in mid-air, body roughly horizontal, limbs splayed. A second, smaller orange monkey is perched among the lower branches and is visible at various points as the view shifts.
visible_changes: The airborne monkey stays in flight for the whole excerpt; its pose changes gradually: forelimbs extend forward and downward, hindlimbs trail backward, and the tail streams out and straightens/curves slightly.

Relative to the frame the leaping monkey holds a near-stable central-right position with only a slight rightward drift and roughly constant height, while the background foliage scrolls leftward, indicating the camera is panning to track the leaper.

The second perched monkey slides across the frame from the lower-left toward the right-middle/upper-right, a change consistent with the camera pan rather than the perched animal moving through the trees.
The leaper's body orientation tilts a little over time (head/forelimbs dipping, hindquarters rising) as it carries through the leap.
outside_clip_unknowns: The push-off and any landing or branch-grasp are outside the segment; the leap is already in progress at the start and continues past the end.
What the perched second monkey is doing (feeding, resting, watching) is not determinable.
The full trajectory and destination of the leaping monkey are not shown.
uncertain_details: Whether the leaper's small vertical position changes are its own motion or camera tracking is not separable from these frames.
The exact 3D path (arc shape, speed) cannot be measured from 2D samples.
The relationship between the two monkeys (same troop, interaction) is not visible.
